heroImageAlt: Sovereign Internal Enterprise Search Agents for Delhi Public Sector Banks with RBI Data Localization
paragraphs: Public sector banks headquartered in New Delhi manage massive archives of internal credit manuals, circular letters, staff handbooks, and board minutes spanning decades. Bank officers spend thousands of hours weekly manually searching through unindexed PDFs and scanned photocopies, leading to delayed loan appraisals and inconsistent policy enforcement. Cloud-hosted enterprise search tools violate statutory banking secrecy acts and RBI on-soil data residency regulations.

Our sovereign enterprise search architecture runs on dedicated private GPU clusters within Indian datacenters (ap-south-1 Mumbai and Delhi NCR). Archival documents are ingested through an air-gapped optical pipeline that handles degraded English and Hindi typography. Dense passage retrieval (DPR) models and cross-encoders fine-tuned on Indian banking terminology generate high-dimensional vector embeddings stored in an encrypted local vector index.

The search state machine processes natural language queries with strict role-based access control (RBAC). Query execution applies two-phase semantic re-ranking: an initial fast vector sweep identifies top passage candidates, followed by a cross-encoder model that extracts exact policy answers with verbatim circular page citations. Zero query text or search history ever leaves the bank's sovereign private network.

Statutory compliance satisfies RBI Circular DOR.STR.REC.11/21.04.048/2023-24 on data localization and the Public Financial Institutions Act. The system delivers sub-45ms search latency across 50 million pages of banking documentation, reducing policy research time by 82% while guaranteeing absolute confidentiality.

faqs.question: Can the search engine understand regional banking abbreviations and circular numbering schemes?
faqs.answer: Yes. The embedding models are specifically fine-tuned on RBI circular formats, Master Directions, and public sector bank credit manuals, resolving complex policy references accurately.

faqs.question: How does the system ensure junior bank officers cannot view confidential board minutes?
faqs.answer: Every document vector is tagged with granular access control metadata verified against the bank's active directory; unauthorized documents are mathematically masked before similarity scoring occurs.

faqs.question: Does the system require internet access for model updates or index maintenance?
faqs.answer: No. The entire search stack, vector database, embedding models, and re-rankers operate in a completely air-gapped environment with offline update capabilities.
